correctness.rationale: Direct chord distances give the stated same-ring and cross-ring maxima. For even n=2m the farthest cross neighbors of U_j are L_(j+m−1) and L_(j+m), with indices modulo n. The cyclic order U_j,L_(j+m),U_(j+1),... exhibits the Hamiltonian rim; the same-ring diameter pairs are n steps apart along it. Their union has an odd cycle of length n+1. Thus a within-part bound strictly below min(A,B) in squared distance is impossible. The rings themselves attain A; alternatively, splitting each within-ring opposite pair gives a bound B since the next-largest same-ring distance squared is 4r²cos²(π/n)<B. At A=B the stated three-coloring separates the chords by using reversed parity on the interior of the second half and a third color at its ends. In either strict regime the farthest graph alone is bipartite (matching or even cycle). For odd n=2m+1, U_j and L_(j+m) are antipodes and the longest edges of one ring form a cycle with step m, hence an odd cycle. This forces 2rc_n and the ring partition attains it. The finite-set diameter-graph chromatic interpretation is exact; monotonicity of the two squared branches gives the unique even optimum and the odd limiting supremum. The last aside of proof step 2 should not be read as a two-color obstruction from the longer class alone in a strict regime: it is bipartite, and only the union is used in that lower bound.
residual_risks: Recorded finite run (253 cases; 303,178 pair evaluations) was inspected, not rerun. Its bipartiteness checks do not independently establish three-colorability, which follows analytically.

value.rationale: A quantitative optimum is determined on a natural sphere family, including a sharp and isolated obstruction to splitting into two strictly smaller-diameter parts.
